Hmm, wait, actually maybe SPACE is "pour": the purple liquid in the frame above pours into the white square below, filling from the top... no, liquid fills from the bottom.
Or, SPACE is "the object above falls onto the object below": the purple rectangle falls and covers the top half of the white square? But the purple rectangle didn't move.
Or, SPACE is "stamp": stamp the object above onto the selected object, aligned to the top edge, with the stamp height being... the purple rectangle is 7 rows; the stamp is 5 rows.
Hmm, 5 rows. What if the stamp height = the height of the selected object minus the height of the object above? 10-7=3? No. Half of the selected object? 10/2=5. Yes, it's half.
Maybe SPACE "splits the selected object in half and colors the top half with the color of the object above"? Weird but consistent.
Or SPACE "colors the part of the selected object that is above the vertical center of the object above it"? The vertical center of the purple rectangle = row 28. The white square spans rows 34-43; the part above row 28 = none. No.
Let me think about the goal from another angle. Maybe the goal is to make the white square completely purple (i.e., the goal panel shows a white square and a purple square as separate objects, and the task is to merge/stack them)? The top-left panel might just be showing the two objects that exist in the game: a white square and a purple square (initial state). The main area shows the current state. Goal unknown.
Maybe the goal is: move the purple square (inside the frame) out of the frame and place it on top of the white square, so that the white square is covered... the top-left panel shows white on top of purple, i.e., a stack of white square on top of purple square. Currently in the main area: purple on top (inside the frame), white on bottom. To match the panel: white on top, purple on bottom. So I need to swap the two!
So the task is: swap the positions of the purple and white squares. The purple is trapped in the gray frame. How to swap? Maybe SPACE "pours"/transfers: when the purple is directly above the white, pressing SPACE moves the purple down onto the white... but the white square is 10x10 and the purple is 12x7 — different sizes.
Hmm, wait. Let me look at the sizes again:
- Purple rectangle: 12 wide x 7 tall (rows 25-31, cols 26-37).
- White square: 10x10 (rows 34-43, cols 27-36).
- Goal panel: white 10x5 on top, purple 10x5 on bottom (each 50px).
Interesting: the goal panel's halves are 10 wide x 5 tall each — exactly matching the halves of the 10x10 square in the main area! So the goal panel is a 10x10 square: top half white, bottom half purple. The main square is currently top half purple, bottom half white.
So the goal is: the main 10x10 square must be top half white, bottom half purple. Currently it's the opposite. I need to flip the colors of the halves.
How? The purple source is the container above. SPACE poured purple into the top half. Maybe SPACE pours into the half of the selected object that is closer to the source? The source (purple rectangle) is above, so it pours into the top half. To fill the bottom half, the purple source would have to be below the white square. Can I move the purple container? It's trapped in the frame.
Or, SPACE might fill the half of the selected object that is farther from the source... no, the top half got filled and the source is above.
Or, SPACE might fill the top half of the selected object with the color of the object above it. If I select the purple band (top half), the object above it is the purple rectangle → the top half is already purple, no change (consistent with the no-op I observed when I clicked the purple band and pressed SPACE!). And when I selected the white bottom half and pressed SPACE: the object above the white bottom half is the purple band → the top half of the white bottom half should turn purple?? But nothing happened. Hmm, that contradicts.
Wait, when I clicked (41,31) [white bottom half] and pressed SPACE (step 8), nothing changed. If SPACE colors the top half of the selected object with the color of the object above, then the top half of the white bottom half (rows 39-41) should have turned purple. It didn't. So no.
Let me reconsider: maybe SPACE's effect is: "pour the active color (purple, per the legend) into the selected object from the top, filling half of it." First SPACE: selected the white square, filled the top half with purple. Second SPACE (no new click): selection is... maybe the selection was consumed, or the object was already half-filled so nothing happened. Then I clicked the purple band and SPACE: the selected object (purple band) is already fully purple → no-op. Then I clicked the white bottom half and SPACE: hmm, that should have filled the top half of the white bottom half with purple... but nothing happened.
Unless the selection requires clicking and then SPACE, and my batched [MOUSE, SPACE] worked... it did work (the first SPACE was a separate action after the click). Hmm, so SPACE after clicking the white bottom half did nothing. So the "fill the top half of the selected object with purple" theory fails.
New theory: SPACE pours purple from the purple container into the white container below it (specifically: the container directly below the purple container). The amount poured: fills the white container up to the level of the purple container's liquid? The purple container's liquid top is at row 25, bottom at row 31. The white container's top is at row 34. Hmm.
Or: SPACE pours until the white container's fill level equals the purple container's fill level (7 rows)? But only 5 rows got filled.

Let me look at the pixel counts: purple rectangle 84 (12x7). Purple band 50 (10x5). White 50 (10x5).
Hmm, what if SPACE "poured" the purple rectangle's liquid into the white square, and the pour amount = the purple rectangle's area minus... 84-50=34? No.
Let me try a completely different approach: maybe the arrow keys do move the purple rectangle, but it's blocked by the frame. And the frame is a "wall" that can be removed... how? Maybe by filling the white square correctly?
Or, the game's objective: the top-left panel shows the goal state of the two squares: the white square should be on top of the purple square. Currently the purple is on top of the white (with the frame in between). The frame might be a "lid" that opens when... hmm.
Let me try more experiments with the arrow keys after clicking the purple rectangle: press DOWN (the purple rectangle is touching the bottom of the frame; blocked). LEFT (touching the left of the frame; blocked). So the purple can't move.
What about the white square with the arrow keys? I tried UP after clicking the white bottom half — nothing.
Maybe the arrow keys move a "cursor" (invisible), and SPACE acts at the cursor position. The cursor's initial position is unknown. My first SPACE (after clicking the white square at 38,31) acted on the white square. So the click sets the cursor/selection.
